summary: Re-review of task 21.11 (log-subject hardening) after the rework pass. My attempt-1 review returned CHANGES_REQUIRED with exactly one open finding, 21.11-F1 (MEDIUM, documentation): docs/decisions/ADR-020.md's v1.2 amendment note still stated the pre-fix host-platform Path.GetFileName semantics and the 'control scalars removed' predicate as the shipped redaction contract, and nothing in ADR-020 pointed forward to the new ADR-026 task 21.11 note. I independently inspected the rework and F1 is closed. `git diff --numstat -- docs/decisions/ADR-020.md` is 24 insertions / 0 deletions and `git diff -- docs/decisions/ADR-020.md | grep -c '^-[^-]'` is 0, so the change is a pure insertion and no existing clause, the task 15.4 amendment note, or any other text was edited; the appended '### Amendment note (v1.2, task 21.11: SEC-21.5-02 and SEC-21.5-03)' sits between that note and '### Rejected alternatives', the same additive placement ADR-026 already used. I read the appended note in full and verified every technical claim against the code rather than accepting the worker's account: the dual-separator statement matches ExtractFinalComponent's `Math.Max(path.LastIndexOf('/'), path.LastIndexOf('\'))`, the Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp predicate matches IsNonPrintingScalar's four UnicodeCategory arms, 'every other category is preserved' matches the exhaustive `is` pattern, 'the 128-scalar bound applied after removal' matches NormalizeFileName incrementing `appended` only for kept scalars, 'the scalar-wise pass that never splits a surrogate pair' matches the EnumerateRunes/EncodeToUtf16 loop, and 'the item-identifier fallback is unchanged' matches the two IsNullOrWhiteSpace guards. The note explicitly records that the old Path.GetFileName / host-native-path and 'control scalars removed' readings are superseded and points forward to the ADR-026 implementation note for task 21.11 (which exists at docs/decisions/ADR-026.md:141) and to docs/architecture/12-performance-and-operational-limits.md (which I confirmed now carries the dual-separator and Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp wording, so the pointer is not dangling). Scope is clean: the whole-diff arithmetic reconciles exactly with the attempt-1 baseline (attempt 1 recorded 9 files / 411 insertions / 41 deletions; the tree is now 10 files / 438 insertions / 41 deletions, and 411 + 24 ADR-020 lines + 3 additional state.json report entries = 438, with the deletion count unchanged at 41), so the only new content is the ADR-020 note, the state.json 21.11 reports list, and the new untracked worker-report.attempt-2.json. src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs (65/21) and tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs (202/2) are byte-for-byte the attempt-1 change and the test file's mtime (2026-09-29 19:42) predates all of 21.11's work, so the product change and its evidence are untouched. I re-ran the focused suite myself: `dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~LogSubjectTests` -> Failed 0, Passed 52, Skipped 0, Total 52. Because requirement 3 asks me to confirm the pre-fix probe still discriminates, I reproduced it rather than assuming: in a task-owned copy of HEAD plus the current test file, `grep -c 'Path.GetFileName(primaryPath)|Rune.IsControl(rune)'` returned 2 (proving the pre-fix source was in place) and the focused run returned Failed 25 / Passed 27 / Skipped 0 / Total 52 across 11 distinct failing test methods, matching the attempt-1 evidence. I re-ran `scripts/check-docs.sh` (nine ok sections, 'check-docs: PASS', exit 0) and `dotnet run scripts/render-docs-state.cs -- --check` ('status.md: up to date', 'PLANS.md: up to date' twice, 'PLANS.md and state.json agree', exit 0) rather than relying on the recorded results. All four files listed in state.json task 21.11 reports exist on disk, the edit is confined to that task's done/reports plus updated_utc (Phase 21 remains status PLANNED with gate 'Gate 21' and tag v1.2.0 untouched), and PLANS.md:267 is '- [x] 21.11' with the generator confirming state.json and PLANS.md agree, so the single-writer table in docs/plan/README.md is respected and no generated block was hand-edited. The worker's report carries all four required fields (acceptance_criteria, test_sensitivity, documentation_reconciliation, interpretations) plus a rework entry for 21.11-F1 with closure evidence that I confirmed independently. All nine attempt-1 acceptance criteria still hold. The single residual is the contract-defined plan-state item the worker itself flagged: docs/agent-contracts.md:22-23 wants the reports array to list reviewer-report.json 'with every preserved .attempt-<n>.json of it', and this new reviewer-report.attempt-2.json is not yet listed. That is a post-review orchestrator bookkeeping step, the same class of item as attempt-1 finding 21.11-F2, it is a documentation-completeness observation rather than a product or acceptance-criterion defect, and scripts/check-agents.sh does not enforce the attempt-<n> entries (it only requires some entry matching 'reviewer-report'), so I record it as INFORMATIONAL/noted rather than holding approval. No user decision is required and no blocker remains.
